title: Punjabi Haveli to Open Fourth GTA Location as Vegetarian Indian Dining Expands
excerpt: The 100% vegetarian North Indian restaurant chain adds a Scarborough outpost to meet growing demand across the Greater Toronto Area.
body:
• Punjabi Haveli, a 100% vegetarian North Indian restaurant, is opening its fourth Greater Toronto Area location in Scarborough
  • The chain offers fully vegetarian menu with vegan, Jain, and Swaminarayan-friendly options, and stays open until 2 a.m.
  • Existing locations operate at Finch and Parkhurst Square in Toronto and on Hurontario in Mississauga
  • The expansion reflects surging demand for vegetarian Indian dining across the GTA's large South Asian community

Punjabi Haveli, the 100% vegetarian North Indian restaurant chain, is preparing to open its fourth location in the Greater Toronto Area, expanding into Scarborough as demand for dedicated vegetarian Indian dining continues to grow across the region.

The restaurant confirmed the expansion on social media and through a listing on its website. The new Scarborough outpost will join existing locations at Finch and Parkhurst Square in Toronto and on Hurontario Street in Mississauga, extending the chain's reach into one of the GTA's most densely populated South Asian neighbourhoods.

A Fully Vegetarian Menu With Broad Appeal

Punjabi Haveli has built a loyal following by committing to a 100% vegetarian menu rooted in North Indian culinary traditions. The kitchen turns out classic Punjabi dishes — Amritsari kulcha combos, chana bhatura, saag with makki di roti, paneer curries, and rotating vegetarian thalis — alongside tandoori specialties, street food favourites, and Indian-Chinese options like vegetable Manchurian and hakka noodles.

The restaurant also caters to more restrictive dietary needs, with Jain and Swaminarayan-friendly options clearly marked on the menu. Vegan diners can find dedicated selections, making it one of the more inclusive Indian dining options in the GTA.

"100% Premium Vegetarian... Serving the GTA, London, Windsor, Niagara, Kitchener, Whitby, Scarborough and surrounding areas."

— Punjabi Haveli

The chain has also introduced fusion touches — tandoori naan pizzas, wraps, and grazing tables for events — while keeping its core menu grounded in the slow-cooked, spice-forward cooking that defines Punjabi home kitchens.

Late-Night Hours and a Growing Catering Business

Unlike many Indian restaurants in the GTA, Punjabi Haveli operates until 2 a.m. daily, filling a gap for late-night diners seeking freshly prepared vegetarian food. The chain also runs a catering division with over a decade of experience, offering more than 100 live stall options for weddings, jaggo nights, baby showers, and corporate events.

A sweets counter rounds out the offering, with gulab jamun, rasmalai, kulfi, falooda, and eggless pastries available for dine-in, takeout, or event orders.

Riding the Vegetarian Wave in the GTA

The expansion comes as vegetarian and plant-based Indian restaurants gain significant traction across North American cities with large South Asian populations. The GTA, home to one of the largest Indian diaspora communities outside India, has seen a steady rise in dedicated vegetarian eateries over the past several years.

For hundreds of thousands of South Asian families in the region — many of whom maintain vegetarian diets for cultural, religious, or personal health reasons — restaurants like Punjabi Haveli fill a gap that mainstream dining options often miss. The demand extends beyond the diaspora, too, as plant-based dining gains broader mainstream appeal.

What's Next

An exact opening date for the Scarborough location has not yet been announced. The expansion marks a steady trajectory for a chain that has grown from a single restaurant to a multi-location operation spanning Toronto and Mississauga, with catering services reaching well beyond the GTA. Punjabi Haveli's Finch location holds a 4.2-star rating across more than 800 Google reviews.
